quizzes.title: India's early-2026 economic data
quizzes.passage:
India's official economic data for early 2026 pointed to steady growth. On 7 January 2026, the National Statistical Office (NSO) released its first advance estimates for 2025-26. The estimates placed real GDP growth for FY26 at 7.4 per cent, compared with 6.5 per cent in FY25. Gross value added (GVA) was estimated to grow 7.3 per cent, with services expanding 9.1 per cent.

The Economic Survey 2025-26 was tabled in Lok Sabha on 29 January 2026 by Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman. The Survey put private final consumption expenditure at 61.5 per cent of GDP, the highest share since FY2011-12.

Price data showed a different pattern. Consumer Price Index (CPI) inflation for December 2025 was 1.33 per cent, a three-month high, up from 0.71 per cent in November, according to figures released on 12 January 2026. Food prices fell 2.71 per cent year on year. Headline inflation stayed below the lower tolerance band of the Reserve Bank of India's target for a fourth straight month. Wholesale price inflation was 0.83 per cent in December 2025, released on 14 January 2026, ending a two-month stretch of deflation.

Industrial output also gained pace. The Index of Industrial Production (IIP) rose 6.7 per cent year on year in November 2025, its highest in 25 months, according to the quick estimate released in late December. Manufacturing grew 8.0 per cent and mining 5.4 per cent, while electricity fell 1.5 per cent. Analysts linked the gain partly to GST rate cuts effective from 22 September 2025. The Index of Eight Core Industries rose 3.7 per cent in December 2025, with cement output up 13.5 per cent and steel up 6.9 per cent. Coal output rose 3.6 per cent, while crude oil and natural gas output fell 5.6 and 4.4 per cent. The index stood at 175.7 points, compared with 169.4 a year earlier, and cumulative growth for April to December 2025-26 was 2.6 per cent, provisional. The core sector data were released on 20 January 2026.

On the external front, merchandise exports rose 1.87 per cent year on year to $38.51 billion in December 2025. Imports reached $63.55 billion, leaving a merchandise trade deficit of about $25.04 billion. The trade figures were released on 15 January 2026.

Inflation policy also drew attention. Under the RBI Act, the government sets the inflation target in consultation with the central bank. The current target is 4 per cent, with a tolerance band of 2 to 6 per cent, for the five years from 1 April 2026 to 31 March 2031. The notification is dated 25 March 2026. If inflation stays outside the band for three consecutive quarters, the RBI must submit a report to the government explaining the reasons and remedial action.

questions.q: Which body prepares the Economic Survey, working under the supervision of the Chief Economic Adviser?
options: Economic Division of the Department of Economic Affairs
questions.explanation: The Economic Survey is prepared by the Economic Division of the Department of Economic Affairs in the Ministry of Finance, under the supervision of the Chief Economic Adviser. NITI Aayog, the RBI and the Planning Commission are not the preparing body.

questions.q: Section 45ZB of the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934 provides for the constitution of which body?
options: Central Board of the Reserve Bank
questions.explanation: Section 45ZB, inserted through the Finance Act 2016, constitutes the six-member Monetary Policy Committee, with three RBI members and three members appointed by the Central Government. The other three bodies are not constituted under that section.

questions.q:
Match List I with List II:
I. Annual financial statement of the Government of India   ->   A. Article 110
II. Demands for grants   ->   B. Article 112
III. Appropriation Bills (withdrawal of money from the Consolidated Fund)   ->   C. Article 113
IV. Definition of a Money Bill   ->   D. Article 114
questions.explanation: Article 112 provides for the annual financial statement, Article 113 for demands for grants, Article 114 for withdrawal from the Consolidated Fund only under an appropriation law, and Article 110 defines money bills.

questions.q:
I. The Directorate General of Commercial Intelligence and Statistics (DGCI&S) compiles India's monthly merchandise trade statistics and functions under the Department of Commerce.
II. The DGCI&S receives daily trade returns from Customs formations and Special Economic Zones.
Which of the above statement(s) is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Both statements are true. DGCI&S, under the Department of Commerce in the Ministry of Commerce and Industry, compiles monthly merchandise trade statistics from daily trade returns received from Customs formations and Special Economic Zones.

questions.q:
Assertion (A): A Money Bill can be introduced only in the Lok Sabha.
Reason (R): The Rajya Sabha can only make recommendations on a Money Bill, which the Lok Sabha may accept or reject.
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: Both statements are true. Introduction only in the Lok Sabha concerns the origin of a Money Bill under Article 109, whereas the Rajya Sabha's recommendatory role arises after the Lok Sabha has passed the bill. The reason therefore describes a later stage and does not explain the assertion.

questions.q:
I. The Economic Survey 2025-26 projects India's real GDP growth for FY27 in the range of 6.8 to 7.2 per cent.
II. The Economic Survey 2025-26 places India's medium-term potential growth at about 7 per cent a year.
III. The Economic Survey 2025-26 projects India's real GDP growth for FY27 above 8 per cent.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Statements I and II are correct, as the Survey gives a FY27 growth range of 6.8 to 7.2 per cent and a medium-term potential growth of about 7 per cent. Statement III is wrong because the Survey's FY27 range does not reach 8 per cent.

quizzes.title: PSLV-C62 failure and the road to Gaganyaan
quizzes.passage:
The Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO) began 2026 with a setback. On 12 January 2026, its Polar Satellite Launch Vehicle mission PSLV-C62 lifted off from Sriharikota carrying EOS-N1, a strategic hyperspectral Earth-observation satellite also referred to as Anvesha, along with 15 co-passenger payloads belonging to Indian and foreign organisations. The first two stages performed as planned, but ISRO reported an anomaly at the end of the third stage, known as PS3. ISRO chairman V. Narayanan said a disturbance in the rocket's roll rate had pushed the vehicle off its flight path, and the payloads did not reach their intended orbit. Among the lost payloads were Theos-2, an Earth-observation satellite built jointly by the United Kingdom and Thailand, and AyulSat, a refuelling demonstrator. The Spanish prototype Kestrel Initial Demonstrator was reported to have transmitted some data.

The failure drew attention because it was the second consecutive loss for the workhorse rocket. The previous mission, PSLV-C61 in May 2025, had also failed owing to a problem in the third stage. After C62, ISRO announced a failure analysis committee. News reports citing sources said a probe had been set up under K. VijayRaghavan, a former Principal Scientific Advisor to the Prime Minister, with former ISRO chairman S. Somanath as co-chairman.

The episode has implications for India's human spaceflight plans. The Gaganyaan programme, which aims to send Indian astronauts to low Earth orbit, depends on a series of uncrewed test flights. In October 2025 Narayanan said the first of these, G1, which will carry the half-humanoid robot Vyommitra, was about 90 per cent complete and planned for December. In June 2026 he said ISRO was aiming to launch it by the end of 2026, though it could slip into 2027. The mission will use a human-rated launch vehicle. ISRO has said that three uncrewed missions will precede it.

Meanwhile, India is also building new launch infrastructure. A second spaceport, intended mainly for small satellite launches, has been under construction since March 2025, with commissioning provisionally targeted for the financial year 2026-27.

questions.q: The Sriharikota spaceport, from which PSLV-C62 was launched, is officially named after which scientist and former ISRO chairman?
questions.explanation: Sriharikota (earlier SHAR) hosts the Satish Dhawan Space Centre, renamed in 2002 in memory of Prof. Satish Dhawan, former ISRO chairman.

questions.q:
Assertion (A): India's planned second spaceport at Kulasekarapattinam is intended mainly for launching small satellites on the SSLV.
Reason (R): A launch site on the southern tip of the peninsula lets rockets fly directly south to polar orbits, avoiding the curved trajectory that Sriharikota launches need to stay clear of Sri Lanka.
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: Kulasekarapattinam is planned for SSLV launches to Sun-synchronous polar orbits; its southern location allows a straight southward path, whereas launches from Sriharikota have to curve to avoid Sri Lanka.

questions.q:
Match List I with List II:
I. ISRO headquarters   ->   A. Thiruvananthapuram
II. Vikram Sarabhai Space Centre (lead centre for launch vehicles)   ->   B. Bengaluru
III. Satish Dhawan Space Centre (Sriharikota)   ->   C. Tirupati district, Andhra Pradesh
IV. Kulasekarapattinam spaceport (under construction)   ->   D. Thoothukudi district, Tamil Nadu
questions.explanation: ISRO is headquartered in Bengaluru; VSSC is in Thiruvananthapuram; Sriharikota island lies in Tirupati district of Andhra Pradesh; Kulasekarapattinam is in Thoothukudi district, Tamil Nadu.

questions.q:
I. The PSLV is a four-stage vehicle whose third stage (PS3) uses solid propellant.
II. The very first PSLV flight, PSLV-D1 on 20 September 1993, successfully placed its satellite in orbit.
Which of the above statement(s) is/are correct?
questions.explanation: PSLV alternates solid-liquid-solid-liquid, so PS3 is solid (HTPB-based). PSLV-D1 in 1993 failed because of an attitude-control problem at stage separation, so the satellite was not placed in orbit.

questions.q:
I. ISRO was formed on 15 August 1969, succeeding the Indian National Committee for Space Research (INCOSPAR) set up in 1962.
II. ISRO's headquarters is located in Thiruvananthapuram.
III. ISRO functions under the Department of Space.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: ISRO succeeded INCOSPAR on 15 August 1969 and is managed by the Department of Space; its headquarters is in Bengaluru, not Thiruvananthapuram (where VSSC is).

questions.q: The uncrewed Gaganyaan test flight G1 is planned on a human-rated version of which ISRO launch vehicle?
questions.explanation: Gaganyaan uses HLVM3, the human-rated variant of the LVM3 (formerly GSLV Mk III), launched from the Satish Dhawan Space Centre.

quizzes.title: Portugal Joins the Artemis Accords
quizzes.passage: Portugal became the 60th signatory to the Artemis Accords in January 2026. Helena Canhão, Portugal's Secretary of State for Science and Innovation, signed the accords on behalf of the country on 11 January. A ceremony in Lisbon was attended by John J. Arrigo, the United States Ambassador to Portugal, and Hugo Costa, executive director of the Portuguese Space Agency. The event coincided with a semi-annual meeting on cooperation between the United States and Portugal. NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman welcomed Portugal as the newest signatory. Arrigo called Portugal's decision a meaningful step forward for responsible space exploration. Costa said that 2026 is the year humans return to the Moon, which will mark the beginning of a new era of space exploration, recalling Portuguese explorers such as Magellan.

questions.q: Who was the commander of NASA's Artemis II crewed mission?
questions.explanation: Reid Wiseman commanded Artemis II, which launched in April 2026. The other three names are Apollo-era astronauts who did not fly on Artemis II.

questions.q: Which of the following countries was NOT among the original signatories of the Artemis Accords?
questions.explanation: The original signatories were Australia, Canada, Italy, Japan, Luxembourg, the UAE, the UK and the US. France was not among them.

questions.q:
Match List I with List II:
I. Year in which the Artemis Accords were launched   ->   A. 1967
II. Year of the Outer Space Treaty on which the Accords' principles are grounded   ->   B. 2020
III. Number of original signatories of the Artemis Accords   ->   C. 8
IV. Number of principles in the Artemis Accords   ->   D. 10
questions.explanation: The Accords were launched in 2020 (B) by eight original signatories (C). They set out ten principles (D) and are grounded in the 1967 Outer Space Treaty (A).

questions.q:
Assertion (A): The Artemis Accords are a legally binding treaty that the UN Security Council enforces against any signatory that breaks them.
Reason (R): The Artemis Accords are non-binding and provide no formal means of enforcement.
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: Assertion is false: the Accords are not a binding treaty and the UN Security Council does not enforce them. Reason is true: the Accords are non-binding and have no formal enforcement mechanism, unlike the Outer Space Treaty.

questions.q:
1. The Artemis II mission lifted off on 1 April 2026.
2. Artemis II was a crewed flight around the Moon that did not land on it.
3. Artemis II landed astronauts on the lunar surface.
4. Artemis II launched from Vandenberg Space Force Base in California.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.explanation: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is false because Artemis II was a flyby without landing, and statement 4 is false because the launch was from Kennedy Space Center in Florida. Two statements are correct, so the answer is 'Only two'.

questions.q:
I. The North Atlantic Treaty was signed on 4 April 1949.
II. The North Atlantic Treaty entered into force on 1 January 1950.
III. Portugal was one of the original signatories of the North Atlantic Treaty.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Statements I and III are true. The treaty was signed on 4 April 1949 and Portugal was an original signatory. Statement II is false because the treaty entered into force on 24 August 1949.

questions.q: Name the strategic hyperspectral satellite also called Anvesha.

questions.q: How many co-passenger payloads did PSLV-C62 carry?
